findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === always false
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable the code tests `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` to detect an empty/full-day-block override. `dayjs()` returns a new object every call, so `===` compares object identity and is never true. The intended unavailable-day case is therefore never detected, and a date override meant to block the whole day falls through to the `dateOverrideExist` path and can incorrectly return available.

findings.title: Working-hours end check uses slot start instead of slot end
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable both `start` and `end` are computed from `slotStartTime.hour()*60+slotStartTime.minute()`. `end` never adds `eventLength` (unlike `slotEndTime` computed above). A slot starting inside working hours but ending outside is therefore accepted. Combined with the fixed-host filter added by this PR, this allows bookings that overrun working hours and date-override boundaries.

findings.title: Availability re-check uses UTC day/time instead of organizer timezone
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable converts the slot to UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`) and then tests `workingHour.days.includes(slotStartTime.day())` and `slotStartTime.hour()/minute()` against per-user `workingHours`, and matches date overrides after an inverted `utcOffset` adjustment (`utcOffset()* -1` then `add`). Working hours and date-override days are defined in the organizer/schedule timezone, not UTC. Near midnight and across timezones the UTC day/hour differs from the organizer-local day/hour, so slots are accepted/rejected on the wrong day and the claimed timezone fix does not hold. It also means a fixed host with no working hours that day matches nothing in `find` and falls through to the busy check returning true, leaving round-robin slots bookable when the fixed host is unavailable.

findings.title: Date-override day matching and time shift drops day overflow
findings.body: getSlots selects `activeOverrides` with `dayjs.utc(override.start).isBetween(startOfInviteeDay, startOfInviteeDay.endOf('day'))` where `startOfInviteeDay` is midnight in the invitee timezone, mixing a UTC instant with a zoned day boundary so overrides are attributed to the wrong invitee day. The subsequent offset correction only keeps `hour()*60+minute()` after shifting, discarding any day carry. An override that shifts to the previous/next day in the invitee timezone is therefore rendered on the wrong day or with wrapped hours, and multi-day/cross-midnight overrides are clipped.
